description:
## Summary

- Restores the MCP-spec GET /mcp server→client SSE stream on both Python and Rust gateways, with multi-node fanout via Redis Pub/Sub.
- Introduces `ServerEventBus` (in-memory + Redis backends), per-session single-listener claim, server-initiated request correlation with holder tasks, body-peek + replay-and-defer, and a session-ownership gate on GET/POST-interception paths.
- Adds ~1.8k lines of focused unit coverage (~828 tests) across 23 files / +6,197 / -196.

Design: `docs/docs/architecture/adr/052-get-stream-and-server-initiated-requests.md`  
Operator quickstart: `docs/docs/architecture/get-stream-quickstart.md`

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/transports/ tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_notification_service.py tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_session_affinity.py` — 828 tests pass
- [x] ADR-052 deny-path tests (non-owner 403, unknown 404, response-interception ownership gate)
- [x] Body-peek over-cap no-double-buffer (`replay_tail is huge` identity check)
- [x] Atomic store+publish via Lua (reconnect-replay race closed)
- [x] Best-effort evict after publish failure with three-way log classification (orphan cleaned / nothing to clean / couldn't verify)
- [x] Cross-stream-id replay rejection, evicted-cursor, no-cursor buffer replay
- [x] Heartbeat-loss preemption + reclaim, preempt-then-late-claim gap delivery
- [x] `bus_iter.aclose` fires on disconnect
- [x] Authenticated + unauthenticated GET to `oauth_enabled` server
- [x] SessionAffinity Redis branches (claim / heartbeat / release × success / conflict / unavailable / exception)
- [x] Bounded `NotificationService.shutdown` timeout branch
- [x] `_bucket_method_label` allowlist caps Prometheus cardinality
- [x] `_accepts_event_stream` RFC-7231 Accept parser
- [ ] Integration: verify against docker-compose edge-mode protocol-compliance matrix
- [ ] Integration: observe `server_event_bus_publish_failed_total{reason}` during a simulated Redis outage

## Out of scope (filed for follow-up)

- [#4332](https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/4332) — `RedisServerEventBus` pump / sentinel / dedup fakeredis coverage
- [#4334](https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/4334) — Split listener-claim methods out of `SessionAffinity` into `SessionPresence`
- [#4344](https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/4344) — `SessionFactory` typed-handle refactor

commits.message:
feat(transport): restore GET /mcp server-to-client stream (ADR-052)

Restores the spec-conformant Streamable HTTP server→client SSE channel
on both the Python and Rust gateways, with multi-node fanout via Redis
Pub/Sub. Design captured in
``docs/docs/architecture/adr/052-get-stream-and-server-initiated-requests.md``
and the operator quickstart in
``docs/docs/architecture/get-stream-quickstart.md``.

Core surface
------------

* ``mcpgateway/transports/server_event_bus.py`` (new) — per-session
  event bus with ``InMemoryServerEventBus`` (single-node) and
  ``RedisServerEventBus`` (multi-node Pub/Sub + ring-buffer event
  store) backends. Distinct ``BusBackendError`` /
  ``ListenerBacklogOverflow`` sentinels distinguish backend outage
  from slow-consumer overflow; ``_force_sentinel`` drain-and-retries
  the wake-up so a slow listener can't deadlock the pump. Overflow
  events increment a dedicated counter; publish failures get a
  ``reason`` label so operators can split backend-unavailable from
  transport errors. Subscribe handles ``pubsub.subscribe`` raising
  under its own try/aclose so a transient Redis hiccup doesn't leak
  the pubsub connection.
* Reconnect-without-``Last-Event-Id`` replays every event still in
  the ring buffer on both backends. A client that drops before
  receiving any event ids was otherwise silently missing pending
  server-initiated requests whose responders would TTL out on the
  gateway side.
* ``mcpgateway/services/session_affinity.py`` — single-listener claim
  enforced via Redis ``SET NX EX`` (multi-node) or in-process dict +
  lock (single-node). ``ListenerClaimResult`` tri-state (WON /
  CONFLICT / UNAVAILABLE) lets the GET handler emit 409 vs 503
  accurately. Heartbeat keeps the claim alive; release on stream
  close. Redis errors are classified by type — config/protocol
  bucket (Auth/Response/Data/NoScript) wins the isinstance check
  before the transient bucket (Connection/Timeout/BusyLoading) so
  credential rotations aren't silently logged at debug. Expired
  in-memory claims are purged in all three listener paths, not just
  ``claim_listener``. ``SessionAffinityNotInitializedError`` is named
  distinctly from ``upstream_session_registry``'s
  ``RegistryNotInitializedError`` so callers can't catch the wrong
  one.
* ``mcpgateway/services/notification_service.py`` —
  server-initiated request correlation via
  ``_forward_request_to_stream`` and ``complete_request``.
  Register-spawn-publish ordering avoids the race where a fast
  downstream response arrives before the holder is registered. The
  holder task tracks the primary failure across ``with responder:``
  exit so a teardown error doesn't shadow the original
  ``CancelledError`` in the done-callback log. Upstream id
  collisions emit a specific warning before cancelling the prior
  holder; ``complete_request`` distinguishes "no holder" from
  "holder already done" in debug logs. Envelope-build catches
  narrow to ``(AttributeError, ValidationError, TypeError,
  ValueError)`` with ``exc_info``; publish-failure is split from
  bus-get so programming errors in ``get_server_event_bus()``
  propagate instead of being bucketed as ``transport_error``.
  Request/notification fanout paths share a
  ``_record_publish_failure`` helper so a sustained Redis outage
  ticks the same metric regardless of which path fired. Both paths
  refuse to emit an envelope with empty ``method`` (defense-in-depth
  against malformed wire frames). ``has_pending_request`` snapshots
  via ``tuple()`` so a concurrent mutation cannot raise
  ``RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration``.
* ``mcpgateway/services/upstream_session_registry.py`` —
  ``MessageHandlerFactory`` ``Protocol`` with keyword-only
  ``downstream_session_id``.
* ``mcpgateway/transports/streamablehttp_transport.py``:
  - ``_handle_get_stream``: claim listener, subscribe to bus,
    heartbeat with TTL-derived cadence + failure tolerance,
    replay-from-Last-Event-Id (or whole buffer on no-cursor),
    sentinel-aware cancellation. ``match`` + ``assert_never`` on the
    ``ListenerClaimResult`` consumer gives compile-time
    exhaustiveness. The ``event_gen`` catch-all logs with
    ``exc_info`` so programming errors in the SSE path have a
    traceback.
  - GET-stream session-ownership gate: runs the same
    ``_validate_streamable_session_access`` check as POST/DELETE so
    a caller who knows another user's session id cannot attach to
    that session's server-initiated traffic. Session ownership is
    also claimed in ``main.lifespan`` regardless of the affinity
    flag, so single-node deployments record the owner the GET gate
    needs. Response-interception runs the same ownership check
    before the body peek so a caller can't forge a 202 by guessing
    a pending JSON-RPC id.
  - ``_accepts_event_stream`` — RFC-7231-ish Accept parser that
    honours ``q=0`` as explicit refusal and matches media types
    case-insensitively.
  - Body-peek + replay-and-defer: ``_BodyPeekResult`` (with
    ``__post_init__`` validator enforcing five invariants),
    ``_drain_request_body`` (cap-bounded, no chunk double-buffering
    — the cap-busting chunk passes through verbatim via
    ``replay_tail``), ``_make_replay_receive`` (yields prefix +
    over-cap tail then defers), and ``_dispatch_peek_outcome``
    (single helper for both response-interception and
    notification-short-circuit dispatch sites).
  - Spec-mandated 202 short-circuit for session-less notifications
    on MCP paths.
  - ``_resolve_intercept_target`` caches the notification-service
    *module* (not the function) so tests can still monkeypatch the
    attribute and the hot POST path skips the import-system round
    trip.
  - ``_bucket_method_label`` maps upstream JSON-RPC method names to
    a bounded Prometheus allowlist, preventing unbounded-cardinality
    label explosion from a buggy or malicious server.
* ``crates/mcp_runtime/src/lib.rs`` — DELETE without session returns
  405; comments reference ADR-052; relay path passes the
  Python-served SSE stream through unchanged.
* ``mcpgateway/services/metrics.py`` — new gauges/counters:
  ``transport_get_active_listeners``,
  ``transport_get_events_delivered_total`` (bounded method label
  set), ``transport_get_rejected_total`` (outcome labels:
  ``no_session_id``, ``stateful_disabled``, ``feature_disabled``,
  ``not_acceptable``, ``session_denied``, ``listener_conflict``,
  ``bus_unavailable``), ``server_event_bus_overflow_total``,
  ``server_event_bus_publish_failed_total``.

Configuration
-------------

* ``mcp_get_stream_enabled`` (default ``True``) — operator kill switch
  that returns 405 with ``Allow: POST, DELETE``.
* ``mcp_get_stream_listener_ttl_seconds`` (default ``30``) — TTL for
  listener claims; heartbeat cadence derived as ``ttl/3`` with a 1s
  floor; two consecutive failures tolerated before tear-down.
* ``mcp_body_peek_max_bytes`` (default ``4*1024*1024``) — soft cap on
  the body-peek path. Over-cap requests fall through to the SDK with
  the cap-busting chunk replayed verbatim instead of 413'd.

Single-node vs. multi-node fallback contract
--------------------------------------------

The bus and the affinity layer both pick their backend by
``cache_type``: Redis when configured, in-memory otherwise. Single-node
deployments work without Redis; multi-node deployments require it.
``main.lifespan`` always initializes ``SessionAffinity`` so the
single-listener invariant is enforced regardless of the affinity
feature flag, and ``NotificationService`` is wired with
``gateway_service`` unconditionally so single-node deployments still
get capability refreshes from upstream ``list_changed`` notifications.

Tests
-----

Adds focused unit coverage (~1.7k lines) in
``tests/unit/mcpgateway/`` covering the GET-stream happy/sad paths
(405/406/409/503 matrix with Prometheus counter assertions);
heartbeat-loss preemption + reclaim; Last-Event-Id replay (including
reconnect-without-cursor buffer replay); preempt-then-late-claim gap
delivery; body-peek over-cap with no-double-buffer identity check;
``_BodyPeekResult.__post_init__`` invariant matrix; notification
short-circuit negative shapes (request-with-id, batches, malformed
JSON, too-large, mid-body disconnect); held-responder
``intercepted=True`` dispatch; GET deny-paths (non-owner 403, unknown
404); POST interception ownership gate; authenticated GET to
``oauth_enabled`` server; ``RedisEventStore.replay_after_with_ids``
cross-stream-id rejection + evicted-cursor + no-cursor buffer replay;
``NotificationService`` request correlation, holder lifecycle,
id-collision telemetry, publish-failure reason classification,
bounded ``shutdown`` timeout branch; ``SessionAffinity`` listener
claim concurrency, Redis-vs-in-memory parity + all three listener
Redis branches covered via stubbed client, heartbeat-failure
tolerance, ``_log_redis_listener_error`` classification matrix;
``InMemoryServerEventBus.close()`` sentinel injection;
``_bucket_method_label`` allowlist; ``_accepts_event_stream`` parser
matrix.

Out-of-scope (filed):

* ``RedisServerEventBus`` pump / sentinel / dedup against fakeredis
  — issue #4332.
* Split listener-claim methods out of ``SessionAffinity`` into a
  ``SessionPresence`` service — issue #4334.
* Typed-handle refactor for ``SessionFactory`` (replaces
  attribute-smuggling on ``ClientSession``) — issue #4344.

Docker compose
--------------

``USE_STATEFUL_SESSIONS=true`` and
``MCPGATEWAY_SESSION_AFFINITY_ENABLED=true`` are uncommented in
``docker-compose.yml`` for the edge profile so the GET stream is on
by default in the protocol-compliance test environment.

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>
